name: Grande Ronde River (Troy – Boggan's)
gaugeName: Grande Ronde River at Troy, OR
blurb: Remote basalt canyon in Washington's southeast corner below Troy, Oregon.

sections.notes: Long day. Take out at the public WDFW Boggans water-access site (unimproved ramp) at the SR 129 bridge; Boggan's Oasis next door is a private store that runs shuttles. The put-in is in Oregon, so Oregon boating rules apply until the river enters Washington. Oregon Waterway Access Permit required for non-motorized boats on the Oregon part of the river; since Jan 1, 2026 it applies to boats of any length ($6/7 days, $20/yr). WDFW Boggans take-out: Discover Pass or WDFW Vehicle Access Pass.

putInAccess.operator: Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife
putInAccess.sourceName: Oregon State Marine Board Boating Access Sites (public), 'Troy Access' (ObjectId 287; manager/owner ODFW; facility Boat Ramp; public_display Yes)
putInAccess.note: Batch 2. Troy is in Oregon (Wallowa County). Coordinate is the Oregon State Marine Board's own boating-access point, which lists ODFW as manager and owner, 1 trailered ramp lane and parking. Esri World Imagery (z19, checked 2026-10-25, research/raw/batch2/troy.png) puts it at the head of the gravel access on the south-east bank just upstream (south-west) of the Troy bridge, about 10-15 m from the water through the tree gap; the v1/OSM point is ~40 m away. Legal access: OSMB lists it as a public boating access site (OSMB boat-ramp map), and BLM's Wallowa & Grande Ronde Wild and Scenic Rivers page names Troy as a river access point. The OSMB record has fees='Yes' but USEFEE='No'; fee status is unclear. BLM says free self-issued river permits are required for boating the Wallowa/Grande Ronde in Oregon.
putInAccess.bankSourceName: USGS NHDPlus HR flowline (flow-direction digitized) + Esri World Imagery
putInAccess.bankNote: Facing downstream (flow bearing ~47 on the flowline), the access is on the south-east bank, right of the NHD centreline. Confirmed on imagery.

takeOutAccess.operator: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife
takeOutAccess.sourceName: WDFW Facilities GIS, Boat Ramp layer (feature 250, unimproved)
takeOutAccess.note: Batch 2. Coordinate is WDFW's own boat-ramp feature. Esri World Imagery (z19, checked 2026-10-25, research/raw/batch2/boggans.png) puts it about 7 m from the water on the west inside bend just above the SR 129 bridge. Legal access: WDFW Boggan's page (https://wdfw.wa.gov/places-to-go/water-access-sites/boggans-1058) lists 1 unimproved ramp, open year-round, camping allowed, and says additional parking and river access are on the left (north) bank below the bridge. WaterAccessSites layer (https://geodataservices.wdfw.wa.gov/arcgis/rest/services/WP_RealEstate/WaterAccessSites/FeatureServer/1) shows WDFW-managed, no closure. Discover Pass or WDFW Vehicle Access Pass required.
takeOutAccess.bankSourceName: USGS NHDPlus HR flowline (flow-direction digitized) + Esri World Imagery
takeOutAccess.bankNote: Facing downstream (flow bearing ~163; the river turns south here), the ramp is on the west bank, right of the NHD centreline. WDFW's note about the north bank below the bridge is consistent with this bend.

timing.note: A reviewed speed/flow calibration has not been established. Access and guide information remain available.

mapAuditNote: Audited 2026-10-25 (batch 2). Both endpoints are verified. Troy (Oregon) comes from the Oregon State Marine Board boating-access point (ODFW-managed) plus the BLM river page. Boggan's comes from WDFW ramp feature 250 plus the WDFW page and the WaterAccessSites layer. Banks come from NHDPlus HR. BLM requires free self-issued river permits for boating in Oregon.
